## B2 — M5-0 · The Cosmology ⇄ Gnostic Library

> **direct:** In tenth-century Kashmir, the streams of Indian thought — Buddhist, yogic, Vedantic, tantric — met and distilled into the most rigorous account of consciousness the East has produced. Its claim, in modern dress: reality is a conscious dream, dreamt by the dreamer who is the Self of every self — simulation theory in old garb, mapped with precision a thousand years early. And mapped in detail: the thirty-six tattvas trace the full descent of consciousness into cosmos, body, and self — and the ascent back — so that every register of experience has its station on one continuous ladder, nothing left outside. Six names carry the deepest strata of that map, and they are the bedrock here. **Anuttara**: the unsurpassable — the absolute before anything can be said of it. **Paramaśiva**: the supreme non-dual — light and the awareness of light in one act, the first self-knowing from which all structure springs. **Paraśakti**: the supreme power — the Word-energy by which the One vibrates, names, and becomes a world. **Mahāmāyā**: the great measuring — *māyā* from *mā*, to measure — the power by which the infinite veils itself in finite, knowable form: symbol, sign, code. This veiling is the divine at play — *līlā* — freely concealing its own freedom and goodness for the sake of the drama; and because it can veil that far, the cosmology keeps its shadow here too: a divinity whole enough to contain its own self-inversion, its power to lose and hide from itself. Split the real into good against evil, refuse the dark a place within the whole, and the exiled half does not vanish — it hardens and gathers power. The fall from heaven names exactly that exiling. It is the floor M5-1 builds on. **Nara**: the human — the bound soul in whom the whole drama is lived from the inside. And at the crown, **Epii**: recognition — *pratyabhijñā* — the activity of the bound one recognising itself as the whole, and the loop circles.
>
> **prime:** Spinoza wrote the *Ethics* in geometric order — definitions, axioms, propositions, every proof citing what it stands on. Imagine that book as a living database you can question. That is the Bimba map: the six names above taken as the architecture of the computational system itself — a graph database in which every piece of knowledge lives inside one body, addressed, related, traceable to its sources, held whole rather than fragmented. A map for an entire cosmology, built as a commons: it grows with everyone who works it. And you are on it: Nara is a position in the cosmology, AND a user-profile.
